parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rules for the acceptable use and handling of information and other associated assets must be identified, documented, and implemented.

controls.title: Acceptable Use of Corporate IT Assets

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security measures must be implemented when personnel are teleworking or working remotely to safeguard information accessed, processed or stored off-site.

controls.title: Teleworking and Remote Working Controls

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Clear desk rules for papers and removable storage media and clear screen rules for information processing facilities must be defined and enforced.

controls.title: Clear Desk and Clear Screen Controls

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Off-site assets must be protected, taking into account the different risks of working outside the organization premises.

controls.title: Security of Off-Premises Corporate Assets

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information stored on, processed by, or accessible via user endpoint devices must be protected with mandatory MDM enrollment, AES-256 FDE, and inactivity screen locks.

controls.title: User Endpoint Security, Full Disk Encryption and MDM

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Governance and usage criteria for Generative AI and LLMs must be established per ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF, including AI asset tiering and human-in-the-loop review.

controls.title: Generative AI, Large Language Models and Machine Learning Governance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protection against prompt injection, unredacted PII submission to LLMs, training data poisoning, and unauthorized shadow AI tooling must be strictly enforced.

controls.title: AI Data Protection, Prompt Security and Shadow AI Prohibition

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Conflicting responsibilities and operational duties must be separated to prevent fraud, accidental errors, and circumvention of organizational security controls.

controls.title: Segregation of Duties and Conflict Avoidance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to information, systems, and network services must be controlled based on business necessity, role-based access control (RBAC), and principle of least privilege.

controls.title: Access Control Architecture and Least Privilege

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The complete lifecycle of user identities (creation, modification, suspension, revocation) must be managed through centralized identity provider workflows.

controls.title: Identity Lifecycle Management and Account Provisioning

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: User passwords and authenticators must adhere to modern NIST SP 800-63B standards: 14-char minimum length, passphrase encouragement, compromised password checks, and no arbitrary periodic expiration.

controls.title: Authentication Information and NIST SP 800-63B Guidelines

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: User access rights must be formally reviewed and recertified at defined intervals: privileged access monthly, critical systems quarterly, and standard systems semi-annually.

controls.title: Access Rights Review and Recertification

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The allocation and use of privileged access rights must be restricted, authenticated with phishing-resistant MFA, vaulted, and audited.

controls.title: Privileged Access Management (PAM)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to information and application system functions must be restricted in accordance with granular authorization controls and defined access policies.

controls.title: Information Access Restriction and Granular Authorization

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) utilizing FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware tokens or number-matching push authenticators must be enforced across all workforce logins.

controls.title: Secure Authentication and Phishing-Resistant MFA

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of utility software programs that might be capable of overriding system and application controls must be strictly restricted, controlled, and monitored.

controls.title: Restriction and Control of Privileged Utility Programs

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An accurate, comprehensive inventory of all information, software, hardware, and cloud assets must be maintained with designated owners and lifecycle tracking.

controls.title: Information and Asset Inventory Management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All corporate equipment, access credentials, and intellectual property in possession of employees and contractors must be recovered upon termination of employment or contract.

controls.title: Return of Corporate Assets

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information must be classified in accordance with its value, legal sensitivity, and criticality to the organization into Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted tiers.

controls.title: Information Classification

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Procedures for labelling and handling classified assets must be enforced, including default metadata classification and visual markings on Confidential and Restricted data.

controls.title: Information Labelling and Handling

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Organizational and security records must be protected from loss, destruction, and unauthorized alteration, in accordance with statutory retention schedules.

controls.title: Protection and Retention of Records

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Storage media containing sensitive data must be encrypted, physically secured during storage and transit, and restricted to authorized personnel.

controls.title: Removable and Storage Media Management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All storage devices and hardware slated for decommission or disposal must undergo cryptographically verified sanitization aligned with NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 and IEEE 2883-2022.

controls.title: Secure Media Sanitization and Equipment Disposal

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must plan how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption, emergency operations, or disaster recovery.

controls.title: Information Security During Disruption and Emergency Operations

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ICT readiness must be planned, implemented, maintained, and tested based on business continuity objectives (RTO, RPO) and resilience requirements.

controls.title: ICT Readiness for Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information processing facilities must be implemented with redundancy sufficient to meet availability requirements and eliminate single points of failure.

controls.title: Redundancy of Processing Facilities and High Availability

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Business impact analysis (BIA) must be conducted to establish recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) for all critical systems.

controls.title: Business Impact Analysis and Recovery Objectives (RTO/RPO)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Formal transfer policies, procedures, and controls must be in place to protect the transfer of information through the use of all types of communications facilities.

controls.title: Information Transfer Policies and Agreements

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cables carrying power, data, or supporting information services must be protected from interception, interference, or physical damage.

controls.title: Cabling Security and Telecommunications Protection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Networks must be secured, managed, and controlled to protect information in systems and applications, including next-generation firewalls at all ingress/egress points.

controls.title: Network Security Architecture and Boundary Protection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security mechanisms, service levels, and service requirements of network services must be identified, implemented, and monitored.

controls.title: Security of Managed Network Services and Connectivity

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Groups of information services, users, and information systems must be segregated on networks, isolating production VPCs from testing and office networks.

controls.title: Network Segregation, VPC Isolation and Micro-segmentation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to external websites must be managed using DNS and URL filtering to reduce exposure to malicious content, C2 servers, and credential phishing.

controls.title: Web Filtering, DNS Security and Anti-Phishing Controls

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cryptographic algorithms and key management practices must align with NIST SP 800-57, including AES-256 for data at rest, annual symmetric key rotation, and automated KMS lifecycle controls.

controls.title: Cryptographic Controls and Key Management Lifecycle

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All communications across public networks or between data centers must utilize TLS 1.3 (or TLS 1.2 with PFS cipher suites), disabling deprecated legacy protocols.

controls.title: Data Encryption in Transit and TLS Configuration

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization maintains cryptographic agility and tracks migration to NIST post-quantum cryptographic standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205), enforcing <=90d lifetimes for TLS and API secrets.

controls.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Readiness and Ephemeral Secrets

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All applicable statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements must be identified, documented, and reviewed periodically.

controls.title: Legal, Statutory, Regulatory and Contractual Compliance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must ensure the protection of personal data and compliance with GDPR and applicable privacy legislation through RoPA, DPIA, and DPO oversight.

controls.title: Privacy and Protection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information stored in information systems, devices or in any other storage media must be deleted when no longer required, fulfilling GDPR Right to Erasure.

controls.title: Information Deletion and Right to Erasure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data masking, pseudonymization, and tokenization techniques must be applied to protect sensitive personal and business data in non-production environments.

controls.title: Data Masking, Pseudonymization and Anonymization

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data leakage prevention measures must be applied to systems, networks and any other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.

controls.title: Data Leakage Prevention (DLP) and Exfiltration Safeguards

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive set of information security policies, governance structures, and management commitments must be established, approved by executive leadership, published, and reviewed at planned intervals.

controls.title: Information Security Policy Framework

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information security roles and responsibilities must be explicitly defined, allocated to competent personnel, and communicated across the organization.

controls.title: Security Roles and Responsibilities

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Executive management must actively lead, support, and resource the ISMS, requiring all personnel to apply information security in accordance with established policies.

controls.title: Management Responsibilities and Leadership Commitment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Formal channels and procedures must be maintained for prompt engagement with law enforcement, regulatory bodies, supervisory authorities, and emergency response agencies.

controls.title: Contact with Statutory and Regulatory Authorities

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security organization must maintain active ties with professional associations, threat intelligence exchanges, and industry cybersecurity forums to remain current on emerging threats.

controls.title: Contact with Special Interest Groups and Threat Forums

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The ISMS and implementation of security controls must be independently audited and evaluated at planned intervals by objective internal or external auditors.

controls.title: Independent Review of Information Security

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Managers and system owners must regularly review compliance of information processing and procedures within their area of responsibility against security standards and baselines.

controls.title: Compliance with Security Policies and Technical Standards

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Standard operating procedures (SOPs) for information security operations, system administration, and infrastructure maintenance must be documented, version-controlled, and made available.

controls.title: Documented Operating Procedures

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Background verification checks on all candidates for employment must be carried out in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and ethics.

controls.title: Personnel Screening and Background Checks

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The employment contractual agreements must state the personnel and organization responsibilities for information security.

controls.title: Terms and Conditions of Employment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All personnel must receive appropriate security awareness education, training, and regular updates relevant to their job function, supplemented by monthly phishing tests.

controls.title: Security Awareness, Training and Phishing Simulations

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal and communicated disciplinary process must be in place to take action against personnel who have committed an information security violation.

controls.title: Disciplinary Process for Security Policy Violations

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information security responsibilities and duties that remain valid after termination or change of employment must be defined, enforced, and communicated.

controls.title: Responsibilities After Termination or Change of Employment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Non-disclosure or confidentiality agreements reflecting the organization needs for protection of information must be identified, documented, and regularly reviewed.

controls.title: Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure Agreements

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must plan and prepare for managing information security incidents by defining roles, responsibilities, severity levels, and CSIRT playbooks.

controls.title: Incident Management Planning, Roles and CSIRT Playbooks

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must assess information security events and decide if they are to be classified as information security incidents based on impact criteria.

controls.title: Assessment and Classification of Security Events

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information security incidents must be responded to in accordance with the documented incident response plan and severity containment procedures.

controls.title: Incident Containment, Eradication and Response

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Knowledge gained from information security incidents must be used to strengthen controls, holding post-mortems within 5 days for Sev1/2 and 10 days for Sev3.

controls.title: Post-Incident Review, Root Cause Analysis and Lessons Learned

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must identify, collect, acquire, and preserve evidence related to information security incidents in accordance with legal admissibility standards.

controls.title: Collection and Preservation of Forensic Evidence

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must provide a mechanism for all personnel to report observed or suspected information security events through designated channels.

controls.title: Security Event and Anomaly Reporting

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information relating to information security threats must be collected, analyzed, and integrated into vulnerability management and threat defenses.

controls.title: Threat Intelligence Ingestion and Risk Prioritization

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information processing equipment must be correctly maintained to ensure its continued availability, integrity, and operational security.

controls.title: Equipment Maintenance and Servicing

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of computing, memory, storage, and network resources must be monitored and adjusted to satisfy future processing capacity demands.

controls.title: Capacity Management and Cloud Resource Scaling

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Detection, prevention, and recovery controls to protect against malware must be implemented on all endpoints and servers, backed by next-gen EDR.

controls.title: Malware Protection and Endpoint Detection and Response

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information about technical vulnerabilities must be evaluated against CVSS v4.0, CISA KEV, and EPSS, enforcing remediation SLAs (<=48h critical, <=14d high).

controls.title: Technical Vulnerability Management and Remediation SLAs

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Configurations, including security baselines for hardware, software, services, and network devices, must be established, tracked, monitored, and automated via IaC.

controls.title: Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code Baselines

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Backup copies of information, software, and systems must be maintained, encrypted, stored in immutable air-gapped repositories, and tested regularly.

controls.title: Information Backup and Immutable Storage

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Logs recording user activities, exceptions, faults, and security events must be generated, stored (90d hot + 365d cold), protected against tampering, and analyzed in SIEM.

controls.title: Audit Logging, SIEM Aggregation and Retention

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Networks, systems, and applications must be monitored for anomalous behavior and potential security incidents, evaluating events against baselines.

controls.title: Continuous Security Monitoring and Behavioral Anomaly Detection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The clocks of all information processing systems within the organization must be synchronized to an agreed reference time source (NTP).

controls.title: Clock Synchronization via NTP

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rules and automated restrictions governing the installation of software by users on operational systems must be implemented.

controls.title: Software Installation Controls and Application Whitelisting

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Audit activities and penetration tests involving checks on operational systems must be planned and agreed between the auditor and management to minimize business disruption.

controls.title: Protection of Operational Systems During Security Audits

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physical security perimeters and access barriers must be implemented to safeguard areas containing sensitive information processing facilities.

controls.title: Physical Security Perimeters and Barriers

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to secure areas must be controlled by electronic access control, visitor badge issuance, log retention, and escort requirements.

controls.title: Physical Entry Controls and Visitor Management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physical security for offices, server rooms, and technical spaces must be designed and applied to prevent unauthorized physical access and exposure.

controls.title: Securing Offices, Rooms and Facilities

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Premises and server rooms must be continuously monitored by surveillance cameras (CCTV) and intrusion detection sensors with retained audit logs.

controls.title: Physical Security Monitoring and Video Surveillance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protection against natural disasters, fire, water ingress, and environmental hazards must be designed and applied across all physical operating environments.

controls.title: Protection Against Environmental Threats

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security measures and guidelines for working in secure or confidential areas must be designed and enforced (prohibiting unvetted photography or recording).

controls.title: Working in Secure Areas

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Equipment must be sited and protected to reduce the risks from environmental threats, unauthorized access, and accidental damage.

controls.title: Equipment Siting, Placement and Protection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Equipment must be protected from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities through UPS and backup generators.

controls.title: Supporting Utilities and Power Redundancy

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information security must be integrated into project management methodology across all product and infrastructure engineering lifecycles.

controls.title: Security in Project Management and Agile Lifecycles

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Appropriate procedures must be implemented to protect intellectual property rights, software licenses, and proprietary source code assets.

controls.title: Intellectual Property Rights and Source Code Licensing

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Read and write access to program source code, build pipelines, and deployment tooling must be strictly controlled, requiring MFA and branch protection rules.

controls.title: Access Control to Source Code Repositories

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rules for the secure development of software and systems must be established and applied to all development activities within the organization.

controls.title: Secure Development Lifecycle Governance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information security requirements must be identified, specified, and approved when developing or acquiring applications, incorporating STRIDE threat modeling.

controls.title: Application Security Requirements and Threat Modeling

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Principles for engineering secure systems must be established, documented, maintained, and applied to any information system development activities.

controls.title: Secure System Architecture and Engineering Principles

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secure coding principles must be applied to software development; peer code review requires at least 1 approval for standard changes and 2 approvals (including Security/CODEOWNERS) for Tier-1/security PRs.

controls.title: Secure Coding Standards and Peer Code Review

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security testing activities must be defined and implemented in the development life cycle, including pre-commit secret scanning, container scanning, and artifact signing.

controls.title: Automated Security Testing in CI/CD (SAST, DAST, SCA)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Development, testing, and production environments must be strictly separated and secured to prevent unauthorized access or changes to the operational environment.

controls.title: Separation of Development, Test and Production Environments

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Changes to information processing facilities and systems must be subject to change management procedures, automated CI gates, and rollback planning.

controls.title: Change Management and Release Governance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Test data must be carefully selected, protected, and controlled; operational personal data must not be copied to non-production environments without pseudonymization or synthetic generation.

controls.title: Test Data Protection and Synthetic Data Generation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Processes and procedures must be defined and implemented to mitigate the security risks associated with the use of supplier products or services.

controls.title: Supplier Security Policy and Risk Management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Relevant information security requirements and Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) must be established and agreed upon with each supplier.

controls.title: Supplier Security Agreements, SLAs and DPAs

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Processes and procedures must be defined and implemented to manage the information security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain, including SBOM validation.

controls.title: ICT Supply Chain Security and Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must regularly monitor, review, and evaluate supplier service delivery and security practices in line with vendor tiering.

controls.title: Supplier Service Monitoring, Audits and Review

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Processes for acquisition, use, management, and exit from cloud services must be established in accordance with the cloud shared responsibility model.

controls.title: Cloud Services Security Governance and Shared Responsibility

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization must direct, monitor, and review the security activities of outsourced system and software development contractors.

controls.title: Outsourced Software Development Governance

metadata.remarks: Centralized canonical control registry mapping internal ISMS security controls to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, AICPA SOC 2 TSC, NIST CSF 2.0, GDPR, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, and ASD Essential Eight.
metadata.title: Canonical Compliance-as-Code Control Registry
